message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today National Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his versatility, athleticism, court vision, and leadership, he has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and has represented the United States in international competition, winning gold medals at the 2008 and 2012 Olympics and the 2010 FIBA World Championship.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also known for his philanthropy—most notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron—and his ventures into media and entertainment, including producing films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment. He remains a prominent figure in popular culture, business, and social activism.
